title_en: Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purposes of strengthening the administration of tax collection, regulating the collection and payment of taxes, safeguarding the state tax revenues, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of taxpayers, and promoting economic and social development.
Article 2 The administration of the collection of all taxes collected by the tax authorities according to law shall be governed by this Law.

Article 3 The levy, suspension, reduction, exemption, refund, and supplementary payment of taxes shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws; where laws authorize the State Council to provide for such matters, they shall be implemented in accordance with the administrative regulations formulated by the State Council.
No organ, unit, or individual may, in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, make decisions on the levy, suspension, reduction, exemption, refund, and supplementary payment of taxes or other decisions that contravene the tax laws and administrative regulations without authorization.

Article 4 Units and individuals that are obligated to pay taxes under the provisions of laws and administrative regulations are taxpayers.
Units and individuals that are obligated to withhold and remit taxes or collect and remit taxes under the provisions of laws and administrative regulations are withholding agents.
Taxpayers and withholding agents must pay taxes, withhold and remit taxes, or collect and remit taxes in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 5 The tax department under the State Council shall be in charge of the administration of tax collection nationwide. The State Taxation Bureaus and local taxation bureaus in various localities shall carry out tax collection administration separately within the scope of tax collection administration prescribed by the State Council.
Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen leadership or coordination over the administration of tax collection within their respective administrative areas according to law, support the tax authorities in performing their duties according to law, calculating the amount of tax payable at the statutory tax rates, and collecting taxes according to law.
All relevant departments and units shall support and assist the tax authorities in performing their duties according to law.
No unit or individual may obstruct the tax authorities from performing their duties according to law.

Article 6 The State shall systematically equip tax authorities at all levels with modern information technology, strengthen the modernization of the tax collection administration information system, and establish and improve the information sharing system between tax authorities and other government administrative organs.
Taxpayers, withholding agents, and other relevant units shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, truthfully provide the tax authorities with information related to tax payment and withholding and remittance or collection and remittance of taxes.
Article 7 Tax authorities shall extensively publicize tax laws and administrative regulations, popularize tax knowledge, and provide taxpayers with tax consultancy services free of charge.

Article 8 Taxpayers and withholding agents have the right to learn from the tax authorities about the provisions of the state tax laws and administrative regulations and matters related to tax procedures.
Taxpayers and withholding agents have the right to request that the tax authorities keep their information confidential. The tax authorities shall keep the information of taxpayers and withholding agents confidential according to law.
Taxpayers have the right to apply for tax reduction, exemption, and refund according to law.
Taxpayers and withholding agents have the right to make statements and defend themselves against decisions made by the tax authorities; they have the right to apply for administrative reconsideration, initiate administrative actions, and request state compensation according to law.
Taxpayers and withholding agents have the right to accuse and report any illegal or non-compliant conduct of tax authorities and tax officials.

Article 9 Tax authorities shall strengthen team building and improve the political and professional competence of tax officials.
Tax authorities and tax officials must enforce the law impartially, be devoted to their duties, be honest and upright, treat people politely, provide civilized services, respect and protect the rights of taxpayers and withholding agents, and accept supervision according to law.
Tax officials may not solicit or accept bribes, engage in malpractice for personal gain, neglect their duties, fail to collect or under-collect the tax payable; they may not abuse their power to over-collect taxes or deliberately create difficulties for taxpayers and withholding agents.

Article 10 Tax authorities at all levels shall establish and improve internal checks and supervision and administration systems.
Tax authorities at higher levels shall supervise the law enforcement activities of tax authorities at lower levels according to law.
Tax authorities at all levels shall supervise and inspect the compliance of their staff with laws, administrative regulations, and the code of integrity and self-discipline.

Article 11 The duties of personnel responsible for tax collection, administration, inspection, and administrative reconsideration in tax authorities shall be clearly defined and shall be separated from and check each other.
Article 12 Tax officials who have an interest in taxpayers, withholding agents, or tax violation cases when collecting taxes or investigating and handling tax violation cases shall recuse themselves.

Article 13 Any unit or individual has the right to report acts that violate tax laws and administrative regulations. The organ that receives the report and the organ responsible for investigation and handling shall keep the reporter confidential. The tax authorities shall reward the reporter in accordance with the provisions.

Article 14 For the purposes of this Law, "tax authorities" means the taxation bureaus at all levels, tax sub-bureaus, tax offices, and other tax institutions established in accordance with the provisions of the State Council and announced to the public.

Article 28 Tax authorities shall collect taxes in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and may not levy, suspend, over-collect, under-collect, collect in advance, defer, or apportion taxes in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
The amount of agricultural tax payable shall be assessed in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 29 No unit or individual, other than tax authorities, tax officials, and units and personnel authorized by tax authorities according to laws and administrative regulations, may engage in tax collection activities.

Article 30 Withholding agents shall perform the obligation to withhold and collect taxes in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations. Tax authorities may not require units and individuals that are not obligated to withhold or collect taxes under the provisions of laws and administrative regulations to perform such obligation.
When a withholding agent performs the obligation to withhold or collect taxes according to law, the taxpayer may not refuse. If the taxpayer refuses, the withholding agent shall promptly report to the tax authorities for handling.
Tax authorities shall pay handling fees to withholding agents for withholding and collecting taxes in accordance with the provisions.

Article 31 Taxpayers and withholding agents shall pay or remit taxes within the period prescribed by laws and administrative regulations or determined by tax authorities in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
If a taxpayer is unable to pay taxes on time due to special difficulties, he may, upon approval by the State Taxation Bureau or local taxation bureau of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, defer the payment of taxes, provided that the deferral period shall not exceed three months at the longest.

Article 32 If a taxpayer fails to pay taxes within the prescribed period, or a withholding agent fails to remit taxes within the prescribed period, the tax authorities shall, in addition to ordering payment within a time limit, impose a surcharge for overdue payment at the rate of 0.05% of the overdue amount per day, commencing from the date the taxes become overdue.

Article 33 Taxpayers shall apply for tax reduction and exemption in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.
Decisions on tax reduction and exemption made without authorization by local people's governments at all levels, competent departments of people's governments at all levels, units, or individuals in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative regulations shall be null and void; tax authorities shall not implement such decisions and shall report to the tax authorities at a higher level.

Article 34 When collecting taxes, tax authorities must issue tax payment receipts to taxpayers. When a withholding agent withholds or collects taxes, if the taxpayer requests the withholding agent to issue a withholding or collection tax certificate, the withholding agent shall issue such certificate.

Article 36 The business transactions between an enterprise or an establishment or place engaged in production or business operations established in China by a foreign enterprise and its affiliated enterprises shall be charged or paid for at prices or fees as between independent enterprises. Where the prices or fees charged or paid are not as between independent enterprises and the taxable income or amount of the enterprise is reduced, the tax authority has the power to make reasonable adjustments.

Article 37 For taxpayers engaged in production or business operations who have not completed tax registration in accordance with the provisions and for taxpayers temporarily engaged in business operations, the tax authority shall assess their tax payable and order them to pay. If they fail to pay, the tax authority may seize goods and commodities the value of which is equivalent to the tax payable. If the tax payable is paid after the seizure, the tax authority must immediately release the seizure and return the seized goods and commodities. If the tax payable is still not paid after the seizure, with the approval of the director of the tax bureau (or sub-bureau) at or above the county level, the seized goods and commodities shall be auctioned or sold off according to law, and the proceeds from the auction or sale shall be used to offset the tax.

Article 38 Where the tax authority has reason to believe that a taxpayer engaged in production or business operations has committed an act of evading tax liability, it may, before the prescribed tax payment deadline, order the taxpayer to pay the tax payable within a time limit. If during the time limit the tax authority discovers clear signs that the taxpayer has transferred or concealed taxable goods, commodities, other property, or taxable income, the tax authority may require the taxpayer to provide tax payment guarantee. If the taxpayer cannot provide tax payment guarantee, with the approval of the director of the tax bureau (or sub-bureau) at or above the county level, the tax authority may take the following tax preservation measures:
(1) Issue a written notice to the taxpayer's bank account opening bank or other financial institution to freeze the taxpayer's deposit in an amount equivalent to the tax payable;
(2) Seize or distrain the taxpayer's goods, commodities, or other property the value of which is equivalent to the tax payable.
If the taxpayer pays the tax within the time limit prescribed in the preceding paragraph, the tax authority must immediately release the tax preservation measures. If the tax is still not paid upon expiry of the time limit, with the approval of the director of the tax bureau (or sub-bureau) at or above the county level, the tax authority may issue a written notice to the taxpayer's bank account opening bank or other financial institution to deduct the tax from the frozen deposit, or auction or sell off the seized or distrained goods, commodities, or other property according to law, and use the proceeds to offset the tax.
The housing and daily necessities necessary for the subsistence of an individual taxpayer and the dependents supported by him shall not be subject to the tax preservation measures.

Article 39 Where the taxpayer has paid the tax within the time limit, and the tax authority fails to release the tax preservation measures immediately, thereby causing losses to the taxpayer's legitimate interests, the tax authority shall bear compensation liability.

Article 40 Where a taxpayer engaged in production or business operations, a withholding agent, or a tax payment guarantor fails to pay or remit the tax within the prescribed time limit, the tax authority shall order them to pay within a time limit. If they still fail to pay within the extended time limit, with the approval of the director of the tax bureau (or sub-bureau) at or above the county level, the tax authority may take the following compulsory enforcement measures:
(1) Issue a written notice to the taxpayer's bank account opening bank or other financial institution to deduct the tax from its deposit;
(2) Seize, distrain, auction, or sell off according to law the goods, commodities, or other property the value of which is equivalent to the tax payable, and use the proceeds to offset the tax.
When taking compulsory enforcement measures, the tax authority shall simultaneously enforce the overdue fine not paid by the taxpayer, withholding agent, or tax payment guarantor listed in the preceding paragraph.
The housing and daily necessities necessary for the subsistence of an individual and the dependents supported by him shall not be subject to the compulsory enforcement measures.

Article 41 The power to take tax preservation measures and compulsory enforcement measures as prescribed in Articles 37, 38, and 40 of this Law shall not be exercised by entities or individuals other than the tax authorities prescribed by law.

Article 42 When taking tax preservation measures and compulsory enforcement measures, tax authorities must act in accordance with statutory powers and procedures, and shall not distrain or seize the housing and daily necessities necessary for the subsistence of an individual taxpayer and the dependents supported by him.

Article 43 Where the tax authority abuses its powers by illegally taking tax preservation measures or compulsory enforcement measures, or improperly takes tax preservation measures or compulsory enforcement measures, thereby causing losses to the legitimate rights and interests of taxpayers, withholding agents, or tax payment guarantors, it shall bear compensation liability according to law.

Article 44 Where a taxpayer who has overdue tax payable or his legal representative needs to leave China, the taxpayer shall settle the tax payable and overdue fine with the tax authority before departure or provide guarantee. If the tax and overdue fine are not settled and no guarantee is provided, the tax authority may notify the exit administration authority to prevent the taxpayer from leaving China.

Article 45 When the tax authority collects taxes, tax claims shall have priority over unsecured claims, unless otherwise provided by law. If the overdue tax payable by a taxpayer occurred before the taxpayer created a mortgage or pledge on its property, or before the taxpayer's property was subject to a lien, tax claims shall be enforced prior to the mortgage, pledge, or lien.
If a taxpayer has overdue tax payable and is also subject to a decision by an administrative authority to impose a fine and confiscate illegal gains, tax claims shall have priority over the fine and confiscation of illegal gains.
The tax authority shall regularly announce the overdue tax payable by taxpayers.

Article 46 If a taxpayer who has overdue tax payable creates a mortgage or pledge on its property, it shall inform the mortgagee or pledgee of the overdue tax payable. The mortgagee or pledgee may request the tax authority to provide information about the overdue tax payable.
Article 47 When seizing goods, commodities, or other property, the tax authority must issue a receipt; when distraining goods, commodities, or other property, it must issue a list.

Article 48 If a taxpayer merges or divides, it shall report to the tax authority and pay off the tax payable according to law. If the taxpayer fails to pay off the tax payable when merging, the taxpayer after the merger shall continue to perform the unfulfilled tax obligations. If the taxpayer fails to pay off the tax payable when dividing, the taxpayers after the division shall bear joint and several liability for the unfulfilled tax obligations.
Article 49 A taxpayer who has a relatively large amount of overdue tax payable shall report to the tax authority before disposing of its immovable property or large assets.

Article 50 Where a taxpayer who has overdue tax payable fails to exercise due claims, or waives due claims, or transfers property without consideration, or transfers property at a clearly unreasonably low price and the transferee knows the circumstances, thereby damaging the state's tax revenue, the tax authority may exercise the right of subrogation and the right of rescission in accordance with Articles 73 and 74 of the Contract Law.
Where the tax authority exercises the right of subrogation or the right of rescission in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it shall not relieve the taxpayer who has overdue tax payable from its unfulfilled tax obligations and legal liability to be borne.

Article 51 If a taxpayer pays tax in excess of the amount payable, the tax authority shall immediately refund the excess upon discovery. If the taxpayer discovers the overpayment within three years from the date of settlement of tax payment, it may request the tax authority to refund the excess tax paid plus the interest at the bank deposit rate for the same period. After timely verification, the tax authority shall immediately make the refund. If the refund involves a withdrawal from the State Treasury, it shall be made in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on State Treasury management.

Article 52 If a taxpayer or withholding agent fails to pay or underpays tax due to the fault of the tax authority, the tax authority may, within three years, require the taxpayer or withholding agent to make up the tax, but shall not add any overdue fine.
If a taxpayer or withholding agent fails to pay or underpays tax due to miscalculation or other errors, the tax authority may, within three years, recover the tax and overdue fine. Under special circumstances, the recovery period may be extended to five years.
For tax evasion, tax resistance, or tax fraud, the tax authority's recovery of the unpaid or underpaid tax, overdue fine, or fraudulently obtained tax shall not be limited by the time limits set out in the preceding paragraph.

Article 53 The State Tax Bureau and Local Tax Bureaus shall turn over the taxes collected to the State Treasury in accordance with the tax collection and administration scope and the budget classification at which tax revenues are to be paid into the State Treasury as prescribed by the State.
For tax illegal acts found by audit authorities or financial authorities according to law, the tax authority shall, in accordance with the decisions or opinions of the relevant authorities, turn over the tax receivable and overdue fine to the State Treasury in accordance with the budget classification at which tax revenues are to be paid into the State Treasury, and promptly reply to the relevant authorities with the results.

Article 55 Where, when conducting a tax inspection in accordance with law on the tax payment of a taxpayer engaged in production or business operations for a previous tax period, the tax authorities discover that the taxpayer has evaded tax obligations and there are clear signs of transferring or concealing the taxpayer's taxable commodities, goods or other property, or taxable income, they may take tax preservation measures or compulsory enforcement measures in accordance with the approval authority provided for in this Law.

Article 56 A taxpayer or a withholding agent must accept the tax inspection conducted by the tax authorities in accordance with law, truthfully report the facts, provide relevant materials, and shall not refuse or conceal them.

Article 57 When conducting a tax inspection in accordance with law, the tax authorities shall have the authority to investigate, from relevant entities and individuals, the circumstances of taxpayers, withholding agents and other parties relating to the payment of taxes or the withholding or collection of taxes; the relevant entities and individuals shall have the obligation to truthfully provide the tax authorities with relevant materials and evidentiary documents.

Article 58 When investigating tax-related illegal cases, the tax authorities may record, make audio recordings, video recordings, take photographs and make reproductions of the circumstances and materials relevant to the case.

Article 59 When conducting a tax inspection, the personnel sent by the tax authorities shall present their tax inspection certificates and the tax inspection notification, and shall have the duty to keep confidential the secrets of the person under inspection; where they fail to present the tax inspection certificate and the tax inspection notification, the person under inspection shall have the right to refuse the inspection.

Article 61 Where a withholding agent fails to set up or keep account books for the taxes withheld or collected, or fails to keep vouchers and relevant materials for the taxes withheld or collected, in accordance with the provisions, the tax authorities shall order the withholding agent to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not more than 2,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 5,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 62 Where a taxpayer fails to file a tax return and submit tax materials within the prescribed time limit, or a withholding agent fails to submit the report form on taxes withheld or collected and relevant materials to the tax authorities within the prescribed time limit, the tax authorities shall order the taxpayer or withholding agent to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not more than 2,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan may be imposed.

Article 63 Where a taxpayer forges, alters, conceals or destroys account books or vouchers without authorization, or overstates expenses or understates or omits income in the account books, or refuses to file a tax return after the tax authorities have notified the taxpayer to do so, or files a false tax return, and fails to pay or underpays the tax payable, such conduct constitutes tax evasion. Where a taxpayer evades taxes, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the unpaid or underpaid taxes and the overdue surcharges, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the amount of the unpaid or underpaid taxes; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.
Where a withholding agent, by the means set forth in the preceding paragraph, fails to pay or underpays the taxes that have been withheld or collected, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the unpaid or underpaid taxes and the overdue surcharges, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the amount of the unpaid or underpaid taxes; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 64 Where a taxpayer or a withholding agent fabricates false tax calculation bases, the tax authorities shall order the taxpayer or withholding agent to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and shall also impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan.
Where a taxpayer fails to file a tax return and fails to pay or underpays the tax payable, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the unpaid or underpaid taxes and the overdue surcharges, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the amount of the unpaid or underpaid taxes.

Article 65 Where a taxpayer who owes taxes payable, by means of transferring or concealing property, obstructs the tax authorities from recovering the taxes owed, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the taxes owed and the overdue surcharges, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the amount of the taxes owed; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 66 Where a person, by falsely declaring exports or by other fraudulent means, fraudulently obtains state export tax refunds, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the fraudulently obtained refunds, and shall also impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of the fraudulently obtained refunds; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.
Where the state export tax refunds have been obtained by fraud, the tax authorities may, within a specified period, cease to handle export tax refunds for the person.

Article 67 Where a person refuses to pay taxes by means of violence or threat, this constitutes tax resistance. In addition to the tax authorities pursuing the recovery of the refused taxes and the overdue surcharges, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law. If the circumstances are minor and do not constitute a crime, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the refused taxes and the overdue surcharges, and shall also impose a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of the refused taxes.

Article 68 Where a taxpayer or a withholding agent fails to pay or underpays the tax payable or the tax to be turned over within the prescribed time limit, and after being ordered by the tax authorities to pay within a prescribed time limit, still fails to do so, the tax authorities may, in addition to taking compulsory enforcement measures to pursue the recovery of the unpaid or underpaid taxes in accordance with Article 40 of this Law, impose a fine of not less than 50% but not more than five times the amount of the unpaid or underpaid taxes.

Article 69 Where a withholding agent fails to withhold or collect taxes that should have been withheld or collected, the tax authorities shall pursue the recovery of the taxes from the taxpayer and impose on the withholding agent a fine of not less than 50% but not more than three times the amount of the taxes that should have been withheld or collected.

Article 70 Where a taxpayer or a withholding agent evades, refuses or otherwise obstructs the inspection by the tax authorities, the tax authorities shall order the taxpayer or withholding agent to make corrections and may impose a fine of not more than 10,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 71 Where a person illegally prints invoices in violation of the provisions of Article 22 of this Law, the tax authorities shall destroy the illegally printed invoices, confiscate the illegal gains and the tools used in the illegal act, and shall also impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 72 Where a taxpayer engaged in production or business operations or a withholding agent commits a tax-related illegal act provided for in this Law and refuses to accept the handling by the tax authorities, the tax authorities may confiscate the invoices or stop issuing invoices to the taxpayer or withholding agent.

Article 73 Where the bank where a taxpayer or a withholding agent has an account, or other financial institution, refuses to accept the inspection by the tax authorities, in accordance with law, of the deposit account of the taxpayer or the withholding agent, or refuses to execute the decision of the tax authorities to freeze the deposits or to withhold taxes, or assists the taxpayer or the withholding agent in transferring the deposits upon receipt of a written notice from the tax authorities, thereby causing the loss of taxes, the tax authorities shall impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan on the bank or financial institution, and impose a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan on the person directly in charge and the other persons directly responsible.
Article 74 For the administrative penalties prescribed in this Law, where the amount of fine is less than 2,000 yuan, the tax office may decide on it.
Article 75 The tax-related illegal income forfeited by tax authorities and judicial authorities shall be turned over to the State Treasury in accordance with the budget level for tax revenue.

Article 76 Where a tax authority, in violation of the provisions, changes the scope of tax collection and management or the budget level for tax revenue without authorization, it shall be ordered to make corrections within a specified time limit, and the persons directly in charge and other persons directly liable shall be given administrative sanctions of demotion or removal from office according to law.

Article 77 Where a taxpayer or withholding agent commits an act specified in Article 63, Article 65, Article 66, Article 67, or Article 71 of this Law and the act is suspected of constituting a crime, the tax authority shall transfer the case to the judicial authority according to law to investigate criminal liability.
Where a tax officer, engaging in malpractices for personal gain, fails to transfer a case that shall be transferred according to law to the judicial authority to investigate criminal liability, if the circumstances are serious, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 78 Where anyone collects taxes without lawful authorization from a tax authority, the collected property shall be ordered to be returned, and administrative sanctions or administrative penalties shall be imposed according to law; if the lawful rights and interests of others are harmed, compensation liability shall be borne according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 79 Where a tax authority or tax officer seizes or detains the housing or articles necessary for the subsistence of a taxpayer and the dependents supported by the taxpayer, the seized or detained property shall be ordered to be returned, and administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 80 Where a tax officer colludes with a taxpayer or withholding agent, instigating or assisting the taxpayer or withholding agent to commit an act specified in Article 63, Article 65, or Article 66 of this Law, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 81 Where a tax officer, taking advantage of his position, accepts or solicits property from a taxpayer or withholding agent, or seeks other illegitimate benefits, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 82 Where a tax officer, engaging in malpractices for personal gain or neglecting his duty, fails to collect or under-collects the tax due, causing significant losses to State tax revenue, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.
Where a tax officer abuses his power and deliberately makes things difficult for a taxpayer or withholding agent, he shall be transferred from his tax post and given administrative sanctions according to law.
Where a tax officer retaliates against a taxpayer, withholding agent, or other informant who accuses or reports tax-related illegal or disciplinary acts, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Where a tax officer, in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, intentionally overestimates or underestimates the assessed output of agricultural tax, resulting in over-collection or under-collection of tax, infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of farmers or harming the interests of the State, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, administrative sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 83 Where anyone collects taxes in advance, postpones collection, or apportions taxes in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, the superior authority or the administrative supervisory authority shall order correction, and the persons directly in charge and other persons directly liable shall be given administrative sanctions according to law.

Article 84 Where anyone, in violation of the provisions of laws or administrative regulations, makes a decision without authorization on initiating, suspending, reducing, exempting, refunding, or supplementary collection of taxes, or makes any other decision contrary to the tax laws or administrative regulations, in addition to revoking the unauthorized decision in accordance with this Law, the tax that should have been collected but was not shall be supplemented and collected, the tax that was collected but should not have been shall be refunded, and the superior authority shall investigate the administrative liability of the persons directly in charge and other persons directly liable; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 85 Where a tax officer fails to withdraw as required by this Law when collecting taxes or investigating tax-related illegal cases, administrative sanctions shall be imposed on the persons directly in charge and other persons directly liable according to law.
Article 86 Where an act that violates tax laws or administrative regulations and warrants administrative penalties is not discovered within five years, no administrative penalties shall be imposed.

Article 87 Where anyone fails to maintain confidentiality for a taxpayer, withholding agent, or informant as required by this Law, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly liable shall be given administrative sanctions by the unit where they work or the relevant unit according to law.

Article 88 Where a dispute arises between a taxpayer, withholding agent, or tax guarantor and a tax authority over tax payment, the taxpayer, withholding agent, or tax guarantor shall first pay or remit the tax and late fees, or provide a corresponding guarantee, in accordance with the tax payment decision of the tax authority, and may then apply for administrative reconsideration according to law; if dissatisfied with the decision of administrative reconsideration, he may file a lawsuit with the People's Court according to law.
Where a party is dissatisfied with the penalty decision, compulsory enforcement measures, or tax preservation measures of a tax authority, he may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law, or file a lawsuit with the People's Court according to law.
Where a party, after the expiration of the time limit, neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor files a lawsuit with the People's Court, nor complies with the penalty decision of a tax authority, the tax authority that made the penalty decision may take the compulsory enforcement measures prescribed in Article 40 of this Law, or apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.
Article 89 A taxpayer or withholding agent may entrust a tax agent to handle tax matters on his behalf.

Article 90 The specific measures for the collection and management of tax on the use of arable land, deed tax, agricultural tax, and animal husbandry tax shall be formulated separately by the State Council.
The collection and management of customs duties and taxes collected by the Customs on behalf of the tax authorities shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 91 Where any treaty or agreement on tax concluded between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries contains provisions different from those of this Law, the provisions of the treaty or agreement shall prevail.
Article 92 Where tax laws promulgated before the coming into force of this Law contain provisions different from those of this Law, the provisions of this Law shall apply.
Article 93 The State Council shall formulate detailed implementation rules in accordance with this Law.
Article 94 This Law shall come into force as of May 1, 2001.
